caption: Figure 10.3: Floquet diffraction-order decomposition with DiffractionMonitor. Tangential fields recorded on reflection (refl_mon) and transmission (trans_mon) planes are projected onto propagating Floquet orders (m, n), separated into upward ('up', +n̂) and downward ('down', −n̂) waves and linear TE (s) / TM (p) or circular (R / L) polarizations. Using the exact discrete FIT plane-wave impedance ensures the sum of order powers equals FluxMonitor.get_flux() to ~10⁻¹⁵.
visual_intent:
Textbook-quality scientific schematic for a computational electromagnetics user manual. Flat vector style on a white background, high contrast, thin dark outlines, generous whitespace, sans-serif labels. Colour code used in every figure: primary grid G, total-field or forward-wave quantities in blue; dual grid G-tilde, scattered-field, backward-wave, or equivalent-current quantities in orange; exact/topological/reference items in dark grey; matched monitor surfaces and conserved-power items in green; truncation limits or unresolved features in red. Colourblind-safe. Every label must be spelled exactly as listed in this brief; mathematical symbols must be typeset correctly (hats, tildes, subscripts, transposes). Do not add any number, value, equation, software name, product name, logo, watermark or title that is not listed in this brief. Prefer fewer, larger labels over many small ones. No 3D photorealism, no cartoon characters, no hand-drawn or xkcd style.

Central schematic of a periodic or Bloch-periodic metasurface/grating unit cell bounded laterally by dashed vertical lines. In the middle sits a patterned grating bar (green). Below at z = −1.5e-6 is a horizontal orange monitor line labelled 'refl_mon (DiffractionMonitor)'; above at z = +1.5e-6 is a horizontal blue monitor line labelled 'trans_mon (DiffractionMonitor)'. From the bottom, an incident blue arrow labelled '(0, 0) incident order flux: inc_power' travels upward (+n̂). Above trans_mon, blue arrows fan out upward (+n̂) labelled 'T_orders ("up", +n̂): propagating Floquet orders (m, n)'. Below refl_mon, orange arrows fan out downward (−n̂) labelled 'R_orders ("down", −n̂): propagating Floquet orders (m, n)'. To the right of the unit cell, two clean callout cards: Card 1 'Polarization bases (get_amplitudes)': 'polarization="linear": up_s, up_p, down_s, down_p (TE s / TM p)' and 'polarization="circular": up_R, up_L, down_R, down_L'. Card 2 (green border) 'Exact discrete plane-wave impedance of the FIT scheme': 'sum of order powers = FluxMonitor.get_flux() (to ~10⁻¹⁵ round-off)'.

Based on the provided methodology section and diagram caption, here is a detailed description of the textbook-quality scientific schematic to be generated:

**Overall Style and Palette:**
The image is a flat, vector-style scientific schematic suitable for a computational electromagnetics user manual. It features a pure white background, generous whitespace, high contrast, and thin dark outlines. The typography is entirely clean, sans-serif, and precisely matches the specified text. The color scheme strictly adheres to the requested code:
*   **Blue:** Total-field or forward-wave quantities.
*   **Orange:** Scattered-field or backward-wave quantities.
*   **Green:** Physical structures (grating) and conserved-power items.
*   **Dark Grey:** Topological/reference items (boundaries, thin outlines, and structural text).
*   *Note: No 3D photorealism, cartoon elements, or unrequested logos are included.*

**Left/Center Region: Metasurface Unit Cell**
*   **Periodic Boundaries:** The unit cell is laterally bounded by two vertical, dashed dark grey lines extending from the top to the bottom of the diagram. 
*   **Grating Structure:** Centered horizontally between the dashed lines is a patterned grating bar colored solid green with a thin dark outline.
*   **Transmission Monitor:** Above the grating (representing $z = +1.5\text{e-}6$), a horizontal solid blue line spans the unit cell. It is clearly labeled with the sans-serif text **"trans_mon (DiffractionMonitor)"**.
*   **Reflection Monitor:** Below the grating (representing $z = -1.5\text{e-}6$), a horizontal solid orange line spans the unit cell. It is labeled with the text **"refl_mon (DiffractionMonitor)"**.

**Wave Vectors (Arrows):**
*   **Incident Wave:** Originating from the bottom of the diagram and pointing straight up ($+\hat{\mathbf{n}}$) towards the grating is a prominent blue arrow. It is labeled: **"(0, 0) incident order flux: inc_power"**.
*   **Transmitted Orders:** Above the blue `trans_mon` line, a cluster of blue arrows fans out pointing upwards at various angles, representing transmitted diffraction orders. They are accompanied by the label: **"T_orders (\"up\", +n̂): propagating Floquet orders (m, n)"**.
*   **Reflected Orders:** Below the orange `refl_mon` line, a cluster of orange arrows fans out pointing downwards ($-\hat{\mathbf{n}}$) at various angles, representing reflected diffraction orders. They are accompanied by the label: **"R_orders (\"down\", −n̂): propagating Floquet orders (m, n)"**.

**Right Region: Callout Cards**
To the right of the unit cell diagram, there are two cleanly formatted informational cards stacked vertically:
*   **Card 1 (Top):** A box with a thin dark grey outline. 
    *   *Header/Title:* **Polarization bases (get_amplitudes)**
    *   *Body Text Line 1:* **polarization="linear": up_s, up_p, down_s, down_p (TE s / TM p)**
    *   *Body Text Line 2:* **polarization="circular": up_R, up_L, down_R, down_L**
*   **Card 2 (Bottom):** A box distinguished by a thin green outline (denoting conserved power items).
    *   *Header/Title:* **Exact discrete plane-wave impedance of the FIT scheme**
    *   *Body Text:* **sum of order powers = FluxMonitor.get_flux() (to ~10⁻¹⁵ round-off)**

*(Note: All mathematical symbols, such as the circumflex over the 'n' (n̂), minus signs, subscripts, and superscripts (⁻¹⁵), are typeset precisely as specified.)*
